findings.where: Hero, the drawn ashlar ground under the words and the mark. Desktop: a vertical joint runs through the R of 'INFRASTRUCTURE', through 'development' and 'infrastructure' in the lead, through the email address under the button, and down through the aqueduct mark. Phone: a horizontal joint runs along the first line of the lead ('I advise development agencies and client'), and vertical joints cross 'on' and 'in'.
findings.fault: The 1px joint lines are the same cut colour and weight as the type. They run straight through the name, the lead, the email address and the logo mark, and nothing holds them back from the words. On phone the horizontal joint lies along a line of the lead and reads as a strike-through. Across the mark it looks like the logo has been cut.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank visitor reading Mark's first sentence sees what looks like crossed-out text and lines scratched through his name and email. Mark would object to his logo being drawn over. Real inscribed stone keeps the joints out of the lettered field, so the stone idea itself goes against this treatment.

findings.where: Nav lockup (the mark and 'MMM INFRA') and the large aqueduct mark in the hero, at both widths; also the palette tile, which lists no logo colour
findings.fault: The client's logo is drawn in the palette's near-black 'cut' (#2A2925), not its own grey arches (#404040) and blue wordmark (#0070C0). This is a one-colour version the client doesn't hold. The palette tile doesn't name the logo blue or grey, either as tokens or as logo-only colours, so a later round can't tell whether the blue is meant to be gone.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose blue-and-grey logo is the one fixed brand asset. The house rule says to change the logo's version or its ground, never its colours, and to make a version the client doesn't hold only with the client's yes. The blue wordmark fails 3:1 on granite, so the tile has to say which version the logo takes on this ground instead of quietly recolouring it.

findings.where: Minium (#86230F) outside the action: the interpuncts between the nav links, the painted 'M' in the texture tile, and the easing curve in the motion sketch
findings.fault: The palette tile labels minium 'the one action', yet the same red also colours nav punctuation, a decorative letter and a diagram line. The tile's own key contradicts the page around it, and the red stops belonging to 'Write to Mark'.
findings.who_objects: Whoever builds the layout round (and Angélique, adding posts) reads 'minium: the one action' in the key and then sees it used for ornament on the same tile. They can't tell which use is the rule, so the red will spread to ornament and the button's colour cue will weaken.

findings.where: Hero, the portrait stand-in frame and its caption label, at both widths; the bottom edge of the hero coursing on phone
findings.fault: The frame's left edge sits about 4px from a joint line, so the two read as a doubled, misregistered line (desktop x≈636 against 640, phone ≈111 against 115). The caption label is inset about 10px on the left but sits flush on the frame's right edge, which gives a doubled rule there too. On phone a stub of vertical joint hangs below the last course.
findings.who_objects: A visitor sees lines that nearly meet as a drafting slip, not as dressed stone. In a direction whose whole claim is precise, laid masonry, near-misses in the linework undercut the craft it sells.

findings.where: Article specimen, the pull quote ('Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on…'), at both widths
findings.fault: The quote's double frame has a heavier outer rule than any other line on the page. That makes a static aside the darkest-edged object in the article, heavier than the section rules, the link's rules and the 'Lay again' outline.
findings.who_objects: A reader of an article page. A boxed, heavy-edged quote pulls the eye from the running text and looks like a panel to press, not a quiet aside. Every post Angélique adds with a quote would carry the heaviest edge on the page.
